fichas.title: Stepped Houses
fichas.summary: Stepped buildings are suited to steeply sloping sites and may step on one or two sides. Terracing can result from setting back units of similar depth or arranging units of varying depth that decrease toward the top. The terraces provide outdoor space for relaxing, working, or play, often with an unobstructed view. Planting parapets can improve residential quality. Stepped houses may also be built on level sites, though lower-floor rooms can lack daylight. Trough depth relates to storey height and the horizontal repeating dimension; recessing a terrace can improve views between terraces.

dimensions.label: Average site slope
dimensions.context: Average slope corresponding to the stacking angle (storey height to terrace depth).
dimensions.ocr_raw: The stacking angle (storey height to terrace depth) mostly corresponds to an average slope of 8–40°.
